questions.question: What is the core promotion invariant for a training checkpoint?
options: It can be reproduced from versioned inputs and improves a protected validation measure
It has the lowest training loss from any run
It used the largest available accelerator
It completed without a worker restart
questions.explanation: A useful checkpoint must be reproducible and demonstrate generalization on data not used to choose its updates.

questions.question: A model fits on one accelerator, but its validated run exceeds the wall-time budget. Which scaling approach is the first fit?
options: Data parallelism with measured gradient-synchronization overhead
Federated learning with every client
Model sharding before profiling
Removing validation to save time
questions.explanation: When model state fits but time is limiting, data parallelism can increase throughput. Its communication cost still needs measurement.

questions.question: Why must a recovery checkpoint include optimizer, scheduler, random, and data-position state in addition to model weights?
options: So recovery continues the same experiment rather than silently changing its update path
So the model needs fewer labels
So validation can be skipped
So more workers can be added without coordination
questions.explanation: Weights alone do not reproduce the learning process; the remaining state controls future updates and the next examples seen.

questions.question: Training loss falls while validation loss rises after several epochs. What is the strongest first diagnosis?
options: Overfitting pressure
A guaranteed accelerator failure
Successful generalization
A need to delete the validation split
questions.explanation: A widening train-validation gap with improving training loss is evidence that the model is fitting training-specific patterns.

questions.question: Validation results are implausibly better than training results from the first epoch, and a feature may contain future information. What should happen before another tuning run?
options: Audit split boundaries and target-derived features
Increase batch size
Add more epochs
Enable FP16
questions.explanation: Potential leakage invalidates the comparison. Rebuild entity and time boundaries before trusting any optimization result.

questions.question: What trade-off does a larger microbatch introduce?
options: It may raise utilization but also increases memory pressure and can require learning-rate retuning
It always improves validation quality
It removes the need for checkpointing
It prevents distributed communication
questions.explanation: Larger batches can improve throughput, but memory and optimization behavior change with them.
